data.note: Half-caster on the Wis ability. The 2024 ranger learns spells from the Ranger list and uses the half-caster slot table (1st-level slots starting at ranger level 2). v0 derive.ts only implements fullCasterSlots — the ranger spell slot table needs an engine-side branch keyed off spellcasting.progression='half'.

2024 SRD 5.2 Favored Enemy: you always have Hunter's Mark prepared (auto-prepared; does not count against the prepared-spell limit) and can cast it without a spell slot a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest. You may still cast it using slots. Number of free casts scales with PB. v0 surfaces the resource pool only; the auto-prepared Hunter's Mark spell and the slotless-cast plumbing need engine support.

activities.name: Favored Enemy: Cast Hunter's Mark (no slot)

data.note: Choose 2 kinds of weapons you have proficiency with to apply their mastery property. You can change one chosen weapon when you finish a long rest. The mastery properties (Cleave/Graze/Nick/Push/Sap/Slow/Topple/Vex) aren't yet first-class targets in the engine; surfaced here as a choice.

Gain Expertise in one proficient skill, learn one additional language, and ignore nonmagical plant difficult terrain. Expertise emitted via choices.expertise; language via choices.language; difficult terrain modeled as a trait flag.

At Ranger 2 the ranger gains a fighting style feat. The 2024 SRD options for ranger are Archery, Blind Fighting, Defense, Druidic Warrior, Thrown Weapon Fighting, and Two-Weapon Fighting. v0 stores the choice; effects are emitted by the chosen fighting-style feat row.
Learn two Druid cantrips of your choice. They count as Ranger spells; WIS is your spellcasting ability for them. SRD druid cantrips: guidance, shillelagh.

Placeholder for Ranger Conclave selection (Beast Master / Fey Wanderer / Gloom Stalker / Hunter in 2024 SRD 5.2). The chosen subclass slug lives on character.classes[].subclass. Out-of-scope for this batch (2b).

Walking speed +10; climb and swim UPGRADE to walk speed (including the +10). SRD: only when not wearing heavy armor — rangers have no heavy armor proficiency in SRD, so applies correctly in practice. Engine cannot enforce the armor gate.

activities.name: Tireless: Gain Temporary HP
activities.note: As an action, give yourself Temporary HP equal to 1d8 + your WIS modifier. Uses per long rest equal your proficiency bonus.

data.note: You can give yourself Temporary HP (1d8 + WIS modifier) as an action, a number of times per long rest equal to your proficiency bonus. Additionally, whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level decreases by 1 (if you have any). v0 surfaces the temp-HP activity with PB uses; the Exhaustion-reduction on short rest isn't simulated by the engine and is flagged as a trait tag.
Choose 2 proficient skills to gain Expertise (doubled proficiency bonus). Engine emits two expertise.skill.<slug> modifiers from choices.expertises array picks.

activities.name: Nature's Veil
activities.note: Bonus Action: draw on nature magic and become Invisible until the start of your next turn. Uses per long rest equal your proficiency bonus.

data.note: Taking damage no longer breaks your Concentration on Hunter's Mark. v0 tags this as a trait; the Concentration-break suppression requires engine support to filter the damage-breaks-concentration trigger specifically for Hunter's Mark.

Moving through nonmagical Difficult Terrain costs no extra movement. In addition, you can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed and without taking damage from them (e.g., thornbushes). v0 tags both effects; the engine doesn't yet model terrain costs or hazard damage suppression.

You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark. Engine cannot check the attack target's conditions during derive(); surfaced as a trait flag — the UI should communicate this to the player. Granting unconditional attack.advantage would be too strong.

You gain Preternatural Awareness: when you take the Hide action or start your turn Hidden, you gain Preternatural Awareness until the start of your next turn. While you have it, no attack roll against you can have Advantage and you can't have Disadvantage on attack rolls. v0 tags the trait; the evaluator doesn't yet strip advantage/disadvantage based on preternatural awareness.

The first time each turn that you hit a creature marked by Hunter's Mark, you deal extra damage equal to your WIS modifier. Engine cannot check attack target's conditions during derive(), and applying the WIS bonus unconditionally would affect all attacks (too strong). Surfaced as a trait flag — the UI should communicate this to the player who tracks it manually.
